reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a specific crypto futures and spot-market arbitrage strategy, demonstrates the trading steps, and explains that funding rates fluctuate. It does promote registering through the creator's KuCoin referral link and funding trading and futures accounts, but the material includes an explicit warning that the stated APY is not guaranteed and does not establish a deceptive solicitation or fabricated outcome.

citations.quote: I will show you how to actually capture arbitrage profit on the Q Coin exchange by hedging the futures and spot market
you will actually need funds available in your trading account and your futures account
you want USDT to be sent to your futures account and then you would just input the amount you want to send and then click confirm
when your spot long position and your short futures position share the same value you can earn arbitrage from the funding fees
the funding rate is actually paid three times a day over here on KuCoin

opening.argument: The video links an income proposition directly to deploying funds and executing a futures strategy. It promises that viewers can capture arbitrage profit, then directs them to hold funds in both trading and futures accounts, transfer USDT, buy KDA on spot, and short the corresponding futures contract. The supposed return is not merely educational background: the speaker says matched positions can earn funding-fee arbitrage, and that positive funding produces payments three times daily. That is a concrete profit-and-action pathway involving account funding, asset purchase, and futures trading, which is characteristic of a trading-return solicitation.

citations.quote: I will show you how to actually capture arbitrage profit on the Q Coin exchange by hedging the futures and spot market
you will actually need funds available in your trading account and your futures account
when your spot long position and your short futures position share the same value you can earn arbitrage from the funding fees
as long as the funding rate stays positive, I will be earning that funding rate three times a day

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this an operational demonstration does not answer the commercial linkage. The speaker does not merely describe a mechanism: viewers are told to fund accounts, transfer USDT, choose an asset, and place paired trades to earn recurring funding. The referral link and fee discount reinforce that participation is being solicited. A conditional statement about positive funding does not remove the fact that the promised benefit is attached to deployment and trading.

citations.quote: Register and trade via my referral link to enjoy 10% discount on trading fees
you want USDT to be sent to your futures account and then you would just input the amount you want to send and then click confirm
you then begin to earn arbitrage from the funding settlements

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited instructions show a trading tutorial, not a fabricated or guaranteed-return scheme. The speaker expressly says the funding rate fluctuates and that there is no guarantee the displayed APY will persist for a year. The referral disclosure is a one-level fee discount, while the demonstrated hedge uses a spot position and a short futures position with a stated condition. Those facts show risk-qualified education rather than proof of deception.

there's no guarantee this funding rate of 0.0529% over on the Kadena or kda token, this token is going to actually stay this high for an entire year
Once that funding rate drops below the level you want to actually earn, then you just simply close out your positions at the same time and look for the next target

opening.argument: The presentation foregrounds unusually attractive returns while directing viewers into crypto futures. The interface displays a 120.68% funding-arbitrage figure and APYs including 66.61%, while the narration describes a 66% annual return as a good return on funds. Those figures appear alongside instructions to transfer USDT, buy a volatile token, short its perpetual contract, and monitor liquidation exposure. Even though the speaker mentions fluctuation, the combination of high headline yields, recurring three-times-daily funding, crypto assets, and account-funding instructions creates a strong risk signal: viewers may be drawn by the return headline before appreciating that the rate can change and the hedge requires active futures trading.

citations.quote: while it looks good at 66% on an annual basis, that would be a pretty good return on your funds
liquidation price would be up at $3.59 almost $3.60

rebuttal.rebuttal: The warning about fluctuation is too limited to neutralize the presentation's most persuasive visual and verbal signals. The platform page emphasizes “Stable Earnings,” displays 120.68%, and lists double-digit APYs; the narration then explains how to fund accounts and trade KDA. Mentioning that rates can fall does not explain execution, counterparty, basis, liquidity, or liquidation risks before inviting viewers to pursue the highlighted yield.

citations.quote: you will actually need funds available in your trading account and your futures account
now as long as the funding rate stays positive, I will be earning that funding rate three times a day

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The visual figures are platform-provided rates and projections, not a guarantee by the speaker. The narration specifically identifies the APY as based on the average funding rate of the last three days and warns that the current rate will not necessarily last for a year. It also tells viewers to monitor the rate and close positions when the reward no longer meets their target. The evidence therefore supports a volatile trading tutorial with disclosed uncertainty, not deceptive certainty.

opening.argument: Although framed as instruction, the video functions as promotion for participation in KuCoin's futures ecosystem and the creator's referral channel. It repeatedly directs viewers toward KuCoin registration, account funding, futures trading, and a specific KDA arbitrage setup, while the description supplies a referral link promising a trading-fee discount. The tutorial framing makes the solicitation more actionable: it walks viewers from having funds, to transferring USDT, to buying spot KDA and selling KDA futures, then presents recurring funding income as the payoff. That is promotional steering into a funded trading workflow, not neutral explanation alone.

citations.quote: Register and trade via my referral link to enjoy 10% discount on trading fees
in order to continue and set up the arbitrage, you will need to come down here to your futures account and click on Trade
the first thing I need to do is buy some KDA
I can short the KDA over on the futures market

rebuttal.rebuttal: The instructional format is precisely what makes the promotion effective: it reduces a financial product to a sequence of clicks and trades, then connects completion of that sequence to funding income. The referral link is not incidental because it offers a direct reason to register and trade through the promoted exchange. Showing the interface and a sample position therefore supplies an actionable participation pathway, rather than merely discussing market concepts.

citations.quote: if you use my link to join q coin you will receive anywhere from 10 to 20 off of your trading fees
The first step is to select the asset you actually want to trade and you go long or buy that asset on the spot market
now I can go ahead and sell short and click sell

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion of an exchange referral does not establish that the arbitrage instruction is a scam. The material explains the mechanics of matching spot and futures positions, identifies positive versus negative funding, and gives an exit condition when the rate falls. Most importantly, it does not claim the displayed APY is guaranteed; it explicitly says the funding rate fluctuates and may not remain high for a year. These qualifications are consistent with an operational demonstration that includes a referral, not proof of deceptive steering.
